articles.title: Wesley Fofana: Chelsea defender booed by own fans in defeat by Nottingham Forest
articles.summary: Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana is booed by his own fans during the Premier League defeat at Nottingham Forest after a controversial interview.
articles.body:
Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana was subjected to repeated boos and told "you're not welcome here" by his own fans during Friday's Premier League defeat by Nottingham Forest .

The jeers aimed at the 25-year-old were heard every time he touched the ball and came after an unauthorised interview with French YouTuber Zach Nani was released.

In that controversial two-hour conversation, Fofana also appeared to joke about missing his penalty during last month's Carabao Cup shootout defeat by Liverpool .

Manager Xabi Alonso said the French centre-back had apologised and "it won't be repeated".

But Fofana endured a difficult time in his side's trip to Forest as supporters made their feelings known.

After Chelsea went behind to a brilliant volley from Igor Jesus in the fifth minute, Fofana also conceded a penalty for the home side's second goal from Morgan Gibbs-White in the 51st minute.

He was booked for the foul on Liam Delap in the box, and then replaced by Levi Colwill in the 56th minute - just after Emmanuel Emegha had pulled a goal back for the visitors - before Gibbs-White made it 3-1 in the 72nd minute.

Emegha scored again in the 89th minute to make it 3-2, but Forest held on to secure their first win over Chelsea at the City Ground since 1997.

Alonso defended Fofana after the game and said in his post-match news conference: "We have to stick together, and everyone that is in the changing room, everyone in the team is needed.

"We need to help, and we need to go through these tough moments all together, and we don't leave anyone apart.

"We need to support everyone. That is because we need everyone, and we need the fans.

"We need all the players. We need to stick together because if not, things will get more complicated, and that's what we want to do."

Asked whether the reaction of the Chelsea fans will make it difficult to pick Fofana going forward, he added: "Well, I'm thinking right after the game, and for the next games, we will see."

Meanwhile, Nani has moved to defend Fofana, saying the player was "clearly" not happy during the interview and admitted he had to perform better.

Fofana also explained he opted to take a penalty against Liverpool as one of the senior players on the pitch, having joined in a £75m move from Leicester City in 2022.

But he confessed football had reached a stage where he was "more unhappy than happy", before recovering physically and mentally.

The release of the interview has coincided with the club's poor run of form, with Chelsea losing 4-1 at home to Leeds United last weekend to make it three defeats in four matches.

The defence, in particular, has come in for criticism, with the Blues one of four clubs to have conceded more than 20 goals in the Premier League after 11 matches.

Having been subjected to racist abuse in the past, Fofana spoke about handling comments during a club-organised interview on this summer's pre-season tour of Asia.

He is understood to be one of the highest earners at Stamford Bridge.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest 3-2 Chelsea: Morgan Gibbs-White brace heaps pressure on Xabi Alonso as Wesley Fofana is booed
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Nottingham Forest beat Chelsea 3-2 at The City Ground; Igor Jesus opened the scoring before Morgan Gibbs-White scored two. Emmanuel Emegha's brace in vain; Wesley Fofana was booed by the Chelsea supporters
articles.body:
Igor Jesus volleyed Forest in front inside five minutes of what was a dismal first half for Chelsea and they never recovered parity. Wesley Fofana - booed by his own supporters throughout - conceded a penalty early in the second half that Gibbs-White converted.

Emmanuel Emegha did come off the bench to pull one back soon afterwards but another goal from the Forest captain better reflected the superiority of Oliver Glasner's side even if Emegha's second in the 89th minute made for a surprisingly nervy finale.

Forest began the evening beside the Trent with only goal difference keeping them out of the relegation zone, but victory lifts them clear of the bottom six. The spotlight now falls on Chelsea, who missed the chance to climb back into the top five.

It is four Premier League defeats in their last five games under Alonso who appears to be scrambling for solutions given the evidence of this team selection. It is not only Fofana under scrutiny at Chelsea. A club in disarray? Alonso needs to get a grip on it and fast.

Liam Delap had been the two-goal hero in the 3-1 win over Manchester City last time out at home and would have been desperate to score against another of his former clubs but it was Igor Jesus' stunning strike that silenced the Chelsea supporters early on.

"It is the first opportunity for them to play together, they have different strengths," Glasner had told Sky Sports beforehand. Igor Jesus' strengths include volleys beyond Emiliano Martinez, it turns out. It was his first goal at the City Ground since April.

Alonso had responded to the alarming defeat to Leeds by dropping Levi Colwill and playing Moises Caicedo in defence. The Chelsea boss changed to a back four as well in a bid to find some form after losing three of their previous four Premier League games.

"Today we need strong characters, big personalities," said Alonso beforehand. "Players that know what it takes to compete in the Premier League." That explained the decision to bring in Danny Welbeck up front, with Jordan Henderson holding midfield together.

But Welbeck was a passenger in the first half, having only seven touches of the ball - half as many as anyone else - while Henderson found himself overrun. Forest were at the back line time and again. Chelsea were fortunate to be only one down at the break.

Fofana had not endeared himself to supporters by giving an unauthorised interview in which he not only talked of being close to quitting football but appeared to joke about missing a penalty in the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool. This performance was worse.

He was culpable for Forest's second goal, bested by Delap before hastily fouling him inside the penalty box in a rash attempt to recover. Gibbs-White slotted home from the spot and Fofana was substituted to the sound obscene chants from the Chelsea fans.

Alonso's side did pull one back through the young substitute Emegha, when Pedro Neto's shot was deflected kindly into his path. But Xaver Schlager's sumptuous ball clipped in behind the Chelsea defence allowed Gibbs-White to hook home his second.

Emegha nodded in another late on to make the decision to omit him after scoring the first goal against Leeds look even more of an error, but it was not enough to earn an undeserved point. Forest held on and are on the up again. Chelsea have problems.

5 - GOAL! Igor Jesus volleyed Forest into an early lead

51 - GOAL! Gibbs-White doubled the lead from the spot

54 - GOAL! Substitute Emegha pulled one goal back

73 - GOAL! Gibbs-White latched onto Schlager's pass

89 - GOAL! Emegha scored his second of the night

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner speaking in the press conference:

"It looks like we are progressing and this is what we all want to see. But also last time [against Man City] was the first swallow [that does not make a summer] and now it's the second swallow and I think everybody could feel it tonight.

"So stay humble, take this feeling of the win and the confidence and the belief but stay humble and prepare well for the three-game week before we face Brighton here.

"We are all feeling again that we are heading in the right direction. Still a lot to do, but every win helps in building confidence and trust. But still 12 points after 12 games is not enough."

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso speaking in the press conference:

"We are working, trying to find solutions, trying to do our best, but things are not going the way we want. And I don't understand any other way but to work, to try again.

"Because if we want to get something, it will have to come from us. No one will come from outside to give us a solution. And the quality that we need, the mentality that we need, it needs to come from within the team.

"Overall, we can do better. I think that we are going through a difficult moment of confidence, things are not clicking, things are not going the way we want.

"We know that in football, this can change quickly, or this can continue. So it's down to us to work and to find solutions to have a better feeling on the pitch and to get better results, because that's what we need."

Asked if he was frustrated with the Chelsea fans booing Wesley Fofana :

"We need to support everyone because we need everyone. We need the fans, we need all the players, we need to stick together, because if not, it will get more complicated."

articles.title: Celtic defend head of security amid Green Brigade row
articles.summary: Celtic defend their head of security Mark Hargreaves and the action taken against the Green Brigade last season.
articles.body:
Celtic have defended their head of security and the action taken against the Green Brigade last season after the fan group declared four supporters had been cleared over the incident that sparked a lengthy ban.

A Green Brigade statement said the four had been "finally cleared of wrongdoing" over the occurrence, which took place during a game against Falkirk on 29 October last year.

The Scottish champions released footage at the time which they said showed "around 100" supporters verbally abusing and assaulting a steward and two police officers.

The alleged flashpoint came after a ticket inspection at the rail seating section of Celtic Park, the club explained, as they outlined a ban on about 250 supporters, which lasted nearly six months .

The Green Brigade say Celtic's "irresponsible and vindictive claim" was intended to "smear" them.

A statement from the group said: "Not guilty pleas were accepted by both Procurator Fiscal and sheriff for breach of the peace charges before the trial commenced.

"The four supporters cleared were subjected to dawn raids, damage to homes and harassment of family members including confiscation of personal devices, this included a vulnerable adult who was left alone in the cold with no means to contact anyone after the front door was removed."

Celtic lift suspension of Green Brigade fans group

The Green Brigade called for the club to apologise for the collective ban and to lift suspensions on two supporters who remain banned over their interaction with head of security Mark Hargreaves at last year's abandoned annual general meeting .

"This week's outcome represents significant vindication for all supporters concerned in these events over the past year," they added.

"It also calls into question the credibility of Mark Hargreaves' subsequent allegations against two Green Brigade representatives."

Celtic pointed out they play no part in criminal proceedings and added that they were not aware all had been completed. And they stated that the outcome of the four cases did not alter their assessment of the incident.

The club said: "The conduct of the group witnessed that day was unsafe and completely unacceptable – it has no place at Celtic Park or anywhere in football. The club took reasonable and proportionate steps to deal with this conduct.

"Such was the seriousness of the incident that the club was called to attend a special meeting of the Safety Advisory Group of Glasgow City Council."

Celtic accused the Green Brigade of continuing a "campaign of personal harassment and abuse" towards former senior police officer Hargreaves.

"Mark is a highly-qualified, dedicated professional who plays a crucial role at the club in ensuring the safety of our supporters.

"Where conduct presents an unacceptable risk to that safety or demonstrates an unwillingness to co-operate with it, the club has to take appropriate and proportionate action."

BBC Scotland have contacted Police Scotland for comment.

articles.title: El Chelsea de Xabi Alonso no levanta cabeza: ¡acumula cuatro derrotas en las últimas cinco jornadas!
articles.standfirst: Los 'blues' volvieron a dejar una mala imagen en su visita al Nottingham Forest
articles.summary: Los 'blues' volvieron a dejar una mala imagen en su visita al Nottingham Forest
articles.body: El Chelsea de Xabi Alonso no levanta cabeza. Cayó goleado ante el Leeds (1-4) -descubrió los abucheos de Stamford Bridge- y ha vuelto a perder, esta vez, en su visita al Nottingham Forest (3-2) en el partido adelantado de la 12ª jornada en la Premier. Cuatro derrotas en las últimas cinco jornadas de Liga podrían relegar a los 'blues' hasta la decimotercera posición. Ahora mismo son octavos a 12 puntos del Arsenal. El plan 'A' de Xabi Alonso, que alineó a Pep Chavarría de inicio y a Moisés Caicedo como improvisado central ante las bajas de Lacroix, Hato y Reece James, no funcionó. A los 5' ya perdía 1-0. Centró Daniel Muñoz e Igor Jesus empató una volea perfecta desde la frontal para batir al 'Dibu' Martínez. Golazo. El tercer equipo menos goleador de la Premier (12) volvía a evidenciar las carencias volvía a evidenciar las carencias atrás del segundo equipo más goleado de la Liga inglesa. Sólo el Crystal Palace (27) ha recibido más goles (23) que el Chelsea. Casi dos por partido. Casi peor que la puesta en escena fue la nula capacidad de reacción que ofreció el Chelsea hasta el descanso. Se marchó al descanso sin tirar a portería. A destacar, únicamente, un tiro lejano de Romeo Lávia en el 24' que tocó en Murillo y salió desviado a córner. Trató Alonso de reanimar a su equipo dando entrada a Emanuel Emegha por Danny Welbeck en el descanso... pero no contaba con la 'ley del ex'... ni la enésima liada de Wesley Fofana nada más salir de vestuarios. Liam Delap, traspasado del Chelsea al Nottingham Forest este verano a cambio de 52,5 millones de euros, 'bailó' al central frances antes de caer en el área. Penalti que transformó Morgan Gibbs-White para poner el 2-0 en el 51'. Fue el penúltimo 'servicio' de Fofana antes de dejar su sitio a Levy Colwill en el 56'. El central, fichado del Leicester por 80,4 kilos, está en el 'ojo del huracán'. "Si fallo, no pasa nada. Si me critican, me da igual. Sé que hay otro partido en tres días", aseguró después de provocar un penalti y fallar otro en la eliminación ante el Liverpool en Copa de la Liga. Al menos Emegha justificó el cambio de Xabi Alonso. El internacional neerlandés recortó distancias en el 54': recogió un 'balón muerto' tras un disparo de Pedro Neto que golpeó en Jair Cunha y fusiló a Matz Sels. El Forest volvió a aprovecharse de la apatía del Chelsea para ampliar distancias en el 72'. Xaver Schlager recogió un mal despeje y dibujó un centro medido para que Gibbs-White superara la salida del 'Dibu'. Emegha, empeñado en darle la razón a Xabi Alonso, estableció el definitivo 3-2 en el 89'. Esta vez el ex del Estrasburgo cabeceó en boca de gol un envío de Pedro Neto. De poco le han servido, sin embargo, a los 'blues' sus tres goles en 113 minutos de juego. Respira el Forest después de enlazar dos victorias consecutivas ante City (3-1) y Chelsea (3-2) en el City Ground. La 'Xabineta', en cambio, ha entrado en barrena.

articles.title: Nottm Forest 3-2 Chelsea: How the players rated
articles.summary: Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice as Nottingham Forest beat Chelsea 3-2 at the City Ground for the first time since 1997.
articles.body:
Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice as Nottingham Forest beat Chelsea at the City Ground for the first time since 1997.

Igor Jesus' brilliant volley opened the scoring after just five minutes, before Gibbs-White struck twice in the second half as Chelsea were consigned to a fourth defeat in five matches.

Forest ran out 3-2 winners despite Emmanuel Emegha twice pulling goals back.

Here's how I rated the players and how you rated the players.

What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean?

Matz Sels: The Belgian goalkeeper could do little about Emegha's goals but did not need to make many saves. 6

Jair Cunha : Cunha made one brilliant last-ditch tackle in the second half as Chelsea pushed for an equaliser. 7

Nikola Milenkovic : The Serbian was solid in the middle of the back three but otherwise unremarkable. 7

Murillo : The Brazilian centre-back made a host of important tackles and no-nonsense clearances throughout. He set the tone for a physical display and had a powerful volley saved. 7

Daniel Munoz : A typically energetic presence on the right, he also set up the opening goal. 7

James McAtee : The midfielder was good in possession but his shots lacked threat. His set-piece delivery was also poor. He did, however, win a few fouls for his team to take the pressure off. 7

Xaver Schlager : The combative midfielder set the tone early by winning the ball back in Chelsea 's half on multiple occasions. He screened the backline well as Chelsea pushed for an equaliser. His wonderful pass through the eye of the needle created Forest's third. 9

Neco Williams : The Welshman battled hard with Pedro Neto in a tactical contest that ended with both players emerging with credit. 7

Igor Jesus : His sensational first-time volley opened the scoring just five minutes into the match, while the rest of his play was neat and tidy. 8

Morgan Gibbs-White : The forward scored his first goal in 11 games against Chelsea from the penalty spot in the second half. He took that chance and then another when played through by Schlager. 8

Liam Delap : The former Chelsea striker proved his worth to Forest by leading the line brilliantly, carrying a threat, looking dangerous in transition and ultimately winning a penalty for his side. 8

Subs not used: John Victor, Netz, Diomande, Yates, Hudson-Odoi, Kalimuendo

Emiliano Martinez : The Argentine goalkeeper was sent the wrong way from the spot and could not have saved Jesus' volley but made a couple of other saves. 6

Josh Acheampong : The young defender played within himself at the City Ground. 5

Wesley Fofana : The Frenchman was booed by his own supporters and told he is "not welcome here". It was a tough end to a horrible week which only got worse as he gave away the penalty having first been caught under a long ball. He was substituted in the 56th minute while also on a yellow card. 3

Moises Caicedo : A shock selection to start at centre-back for first time in his 210 games in English football, the Ecuadorian looked out of sorts with possession and in his positioning. He failed to cover for Fofana before he gave away the penalty. 5

Pep Chavarria : The Spanish full-back was an anonymous presence but did not make any obvious mistakes. 5

Romeo Lavia : The Belgian recovered from a poor touch early on to set the tempo for possession domination and his passes had real purpose. 7

Jordan Henderson : The 36-year-old was one of the weaker Chelsea performers as he filled in for now-defender Caicedo. 5

Pedro Neto : The Portuguese winger showed impressive work-rate competing with Williams, while threatened with his running in behind. His second-half shot was blocked but led to Chelsea 's first goal, while his cross set up his side's second. 7

Cole Palmer : The forward was creative and highly involved for Chelsea but could not deliver that moment. It owed more to his team-mates not performing than himself. 6

Morgan Rogers : Rogers squandered multiple chances, including a huge opportunity to equalise from a corner midway through the second half. 4

Danny Welbeck : The 35-year-old striker had absolutely no service but was also completely anonymous in the first half and was taken off at the interval. 4

Emmanuel Emegha (on 45, Welbeck): An outstanding second-half display, with a brilliant touch and shot to pull one after the ball deflected into his path. He headed in a second at the far post. It raises the question about why he did not start having also scored against Leeds last weekend. 8

Levi Colwill (on 56, Fofana): The England international will be frustrated to have been dropped for a midfielder but was forced on amid Fofana's struggles and did not have much chance to shine. 5

Subs not used: Penders, Gusto, Barco, Nicoll-Jazuli, Estevao

After the opportunity to rate players has closed, the score displayed represents the average from all the submissions by BBC Sport users.

articles.title: Southampton 2-0 Middlesbrough: Finn Azaz scores against former club in ill-tempered first meeting since 'Spygate'
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Southampton and Middlesbrough at St Mary's on Friday night; goals from Ryan Manning and Finn Azaz earn Saints victory in first meeting since last season's 'Spygate'
articles.body:
Six-and-a-half months on from 'Spygate' - which dominated the headlines during last season's play-offs - Saints emerged victorious, as they did in the semi-final second leg, in an ill-tempered affair that saw 10 yellow cards brandished to players and two to coaching staff.

Had it not been for the four-point penalty imposed on them as a result, Friday night's win would have sent them to the top of the Sky Bet Championship.

But goals from Ryan Manning and Finn Azaz - who goaded his former club's fans as he celebrated - put them within touching distance of the summit.

Boro's third defeat of the season opens the door to Stoke and Wolves to leapfrog them into top spot if they win on Saturday.

In the build-up, Tonda Eckert and Kim Hellberg insisted they had buried the hatchet - but neither fanbase had forgotten it. Both sets of players were booed when they came out to warm up, while chants referencing the saga echoed around St Mary's. The atmosphere was electric.

Meaningful chances came at a premium in the first half, but they were high quality when they did come.

The home fans fell silent for a split-second when Will Lankshear ghosted away from his man and moved one-on-one with Saints goalkeeper Daniel Peretz, who denied the Championship's top scorer.

And at the other end, Radek Vitek had to be at his best, first to tip Azaz's fierce strike onto the crossbar, then to push a Cyle Larin header over.

The first goal came just before the hour. Kuryu Matsuki's cross flew over everyone in the box, but James Bree was there to collect and fizz in a low ball that Manning ran onto and side-footed high into the net.

Twenty minutes later, Azaz capitalised on a defensive mistake to calmly slot home the second, before running straight towards the visiting supporters and making a sarcastic crying gesture, sparking a heated reaction.

This is not a rivalry that is going anywhere any time soon.

7: CHANCE ! Ryan Manning finds Lewis Dobbin with a pinpoint cross, but he heads over the bar.

16: SAVE ! Will Lankshear darts away from his man and tries a shot from an angle, which Daniel Peretz repels.

19: OFF THE BAR ! Finn Azaz hits a shot, which is tipped onto the crossbar by Radek Vitek.

38: SAVE ! Cyle Larin powers a header at goal, but Vitek again tips over the bar.

59: GOAL ! James Bree fizzes in a low ball, which Manning meets and sidefoots home.

66: NO PENALTY ! Larin's shot is blocked, potentially by a hand, but penalty appeals are waved away.

79: GOAL ! Former Boro man Azaz rolls home Saints' second and goads the travelling fans, which sparks a melee.

Azaz explains celebration - and has no regrets over it...

Southampton's Finn Azaz speaking to Sky Sports:

"They sang about my family home and away last season, so I was just waiting for my moment to get one back.

Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert in his press conference

Eckert: I didn't like social media post mocking Middlesbrough's play-off defeat

Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert admitted he "didn't like" a social media video posted by the club ahead of the first meeting with Middlesbrough since 'Spygate' last season.

The video included footage of Oli McBurnie's Championship play-off final winner for Hull against Boro at Wembley in May.

It was also played on the big screens at St Mary's in the lead-up to kick-off.

"I didn't like the video this morning. No, I didn't like it," Eckert said in his post-match press conference.

"I haven't even seen the video, I've just heard the information about what was in there and I didn't like it.

"I think, if we look back a couple of months, the reality is that both clubs have lost. One club has lost off the pitch, the other has lost off the pitch. I think it's an episode that is good to close for both clubs and to move forward.

"I've apologised to Kim, I've apologised openly. For me, there is no need to warm that up again."

It was pointed out to Eckert that a box of tissues had been placed on the table behind which managers sit, seemingly mocking Hellberg after his emotional reaction to the defeat in the play-off semi-final at St Mary's in May.

After a few seconds of looking at the box, he said: "You can take this one [box of tissues] off." He then placed them under the table.

"I just love to talk about football and I hope everyone who came here, especially the Middlesbrough staff and players know that," he said.

"I hope they know these things don't come from me."

Hellberg said: "They are always trying to fire everything up. I saw there were some posts at the end where they tried to mock me - or whoever they were trying to mock - so I feel a little bit small about that.

"Otherwise, there's a very good football side, so many good players, the staff are good. There's no need for that, but it is what it is."

articles.title: Pablo García levanta a un Racing que coge velocidad de crucero
articles.standfirst: Los cántabros, que duermen en puestos europeos, remontaron en Valencia gracias a un doblete del sevillano y a otra diana de Zabiri, que ya lleva 12.
articles.summary: Los cántabros, que duermen en puestos europeos, remontaron en Valencia gracias a un doblete del sevillano y a otra diana de Zabiri, que ya lleva 12.
articles.body: El Racing logró con otra remontada su tercera victoria consecutiva ante el Levante en el Ciutat de Valencia en el duelo que abría la jornada 14. Los santanderinos meten la directa y duermen en puestos europeos gracias a Zabiri y a Pablo García, que pide paso con un doblete tremendo. El marroquí, con su gol 12 del curso, culminó la reacción visitante tras el tanto inicial de Iván Romero y el ex del Betis, con dos cañonazos, igualó primero y sentenció después en un segundo tiempo en el que los de José Alberto tiraron de casta y de calidad para sumar su segundo triunfo lejos de El Sardinero. Un encuentro que comenzó trepidante, con dos equipos atrevidos buscando la portería rival desde el pitido inicial. Dos defensas adelantadas que provocaron los primeros avisos serios de Zabiri, que falló dentro del área a los cinco minutos, y de Dela, cuyo cabezazo lo escupió el poste tras rozar en un central. El máximo anotador del Racing tuvo otra en sus botas buscando la ‘rosquita’ al segundo palo poco después, y a partir de ahí fueron los granotas los que pisaron el acelerador a fondo. Requena dispuso de dos opciones de abrir la lata en apenas dos minutos cuando casi se alcanzaba la media hora de juego, pero no sería él el encargado de desatar la locura en el Ciutat. Iván Romero, que poco antes tuvo una clarísima tras un pase fantástico de Olasagasti, no falló cuando el reloj marcaba 42 minutos. Se quedó enganchada la zaga tras un saque de Julen que rechazó Oriol Rey en la medular. La enganchó el manchego y, de derechazo cruzado en la semiluna, hizo el primero para su equipo y el cuarto en su cuenta particular este curso. Un premio muy merecido y que hacía justicia a lo visto en el primer asalto ante un Racing que tuvo momentos de dominio al inicio pero que se acabó viendo encajonado en su propia mitad de campo. Tras el paso por vestuarios, Zabiri volvió a avisar nada más comenzar a la salida de un córner, pero desde entonces y hasta el triple cambio de José Alberto, ambos equipos estaban neutralizándose. Eso sí, uno de los elementos nuevos que introdujo el técnico asturiano fue Pablo García, que puso las tablas ‘a lo Juan Palomo’ recibiendo en el pico del área, abriéndose y clavando un zurdazo descomunal donde no podía llegar Ryan. Con el sevillano habían entrado Almeida y Hugo Pérez seis minutos antes de poner las tablas. Buscaba el entrenador racinguista una reacción… y la encontró con el tercer gol del sevillano en esta Liga. Un diana que volvió a reactivar a ambos equipos, y la sensación que sobrevolaba el Ciutat era que cualquiera podría llevarse la contienda. Eso sí, las más claras fueron de los visitantes… que se lo empezaron a creer. Hugo Pérez, otro de los refrescos, probó a Ryan en el tramo final con un derechazo desde su casa que tuvo que enviar el australiano a córner. Y, poco después, Zabiri ya no perdonó. Lo había hecho un minuto antes con un zurdazo al poste, pero en la jugada siguiente aprovechó la 'pantalla' de Villalibre a Mandi para, con su pierna buena, silenciar el feudo levantinista con un disparo raso cruzado. Duodécimo tanto del marroquí, que está que se sale, y que hace que el equipo racinguista haya dormido este viernes sexto en la clasificación gracias a su tercera victoria consecutiva. Una victoria en la que Julen Agirrezabala también tuvo su papel fundamental con una gran mano que evitó el 2-2 de Brugui antes de la sentencia en los últimos segundos de Pablo García con otro cañonazo de zurda a la contra. Los de Luís Castro lo intentaron hasta la extenuación, pero ya son cinco partidos seguidos sin ganar tras haber sucumbido ante un recién ascendido que ya ha cogido velocidad de crucero.

articles.title: Jack Wilshere and Aaron Ramsey: The Arsenal legends on similar managerial paths
articles.summary: Eighteen years after making their Premier League debuts two minutes apart, Jack Wilshere and Aaron Ramsey meet as managers.
articles.body:
Aaron Ramsey and Jack Wilshere have a lot in common.

Both were midfield prodigies. Both won the FA Cup playing for Arsenal under Arsene Wenger. Both represented their countries.

The image of the pair celebrating Ramsey's extra-time winner together in the 2014 FA Cup final against Hull City to end Arsenal's nine-year trophy drought at the time will forever be ingrained in the north London club's history.

They were teenagers when they made their Premier League debuts for the Gunners on the same day just two minutes apart as substitutes in a 4-0 win at Blackburn in September 2008.

Aged just 16 and 17, each were considered hot prospects who would go on to have excellent careers - and so it proved in many ways, even if both were restricted by injuries along the way.

Now 34 and 35, their paths cross again under different circumstances but many similarities very much still remain.

They are both in League One in their first permanent managerial jobs. And, guess what? Both their sides are in fine form and vying for promotion to the Championship.

It will be the first time they have met as permanent managers when Wilshere's Luton Town host Ramsey's Oxford United at Kenilworth Road on Saturday (15:00 GMT).

Ramsey and Wilshere have both tried to play down their reunion.

"Obviously it will be nice to see Jack again, but it's not about us," Ramsey told BBC Radio Oxford.

Except it is about them a little bit, given their 101 appearances in 10 years together in the Arsenal midfield - and as two young managers who are following almost identical paths.

Immediately after retiring from playing in July 2022, Wilshere was appointed the under-18s head coach at Arsenal, the club where he had risen from the youth academy to the first team.

Meanwhile, former Wales international Ramsey gained coaching experience towards the end of his playing career, also working with the under-18s at boyhood club Cardiff City.

Wilshere joined Norwich City as a coach for the 2024-25 season and it was at the end of that campaign he would first meet Ramsey as a manager in a remarkable twist of fate after they were both placed in interim charge of the Canaries and Bluebirds respectively.

The bragging rights went to Wilshere on that day in May last year as Norwich beat Cardiff 4-2.

"I owe him one from that," Ramsey joked.

Despite their close relationship and working towards the same objectives in the same league, they have not spoken "for a while".

"We are in a similar position at the moment, but I haven't had much dialogue with him over the last few months," said Ramsey.

"We're both fighting for the same things but, for me, it's just going out there to try and win a game of football."

"It doesn't change anything for how we prepare," Wilshere told BBC Three Counties Radio on Friday.

"Of course, when I see Aaron, that'll be a nice moment. We spent a lot of good times together.

"He's had a really good start and credit to him. He's got a football brain, he's got a good career in the game and he's clearly taking that into his coaching.

Since taking over at Luton in October 2025, Wilshere has already tasted silverware, lifting the EFL Trophy at Wembley in April - a feeling he said he enjoyed more as a manager than when he was a player.

The 34-year-old guided the Hatters to seventh in League One last season, narrowly missing out on a play-off spot by a point.

Wilshere slightly edges his counterpart in terms of managerial experience, with 64 games in all competitions as Luton boss, while Ramsey has taken charge of 18 matches in his first season with the U's.

Neither could have their side in much better shape heading into Saturday's showdown.

After a stuttering start to 2026-27, Luton have won five of their past six games (D1) to climb from 16th up to fifth.

As for Ramsey, he is doing a fine job with Oxford considering the club have been under a transfer embargo since he arrived - and says he is "loving every second of it".

His side are on an 11-game unbeaten run - the second-longest across the entire Football League behind only Salford City (13).

With just one defeat so far, Oxford are third and three points behind Stockport and Huddersfield with two games in hand.

The influences on Wilshere and Ramsey are clear to see, both in the styles of play they adopt and the way they conduct themselves.

They have both learnt from the same mentors, particularly Wenger and current Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta, who they also played alongside in midfield.

It is perhaps no surprise the pair have gone into coaching - a common theme among Wenger's disciples.

Arteta, Patrick Vieira, Thierry Henry, Ashley Cole, Robin van Persie, Kolo Toure and Cesc Fabregas have also done so.

Wilshere and Ramsey have both spoken openly about the huge impact Wenger has had on them.

They also give a lot of credit to their role model Arteta.

Watching from afar, Ramsey previously said it was inspiring to see his former team-mate guide Arsenal to the Premier League title and Champions League final.

It was also Arteta who advised Ramsey to take his coaching badges and has continued to help him along the way.

But for Wilshere, he got to learn first hand from the Spaniard on the training ground.

"I got to see Mikel and how he coached and the influence he was having," Wilshere said last month.

"I would ask him questions, why he's doing certain things, and I started to fall in love with it and how he started to prepare training sessions.

"I was influenced by Mikel, but then I had to learn how to teach. I had to learn how to get that across, how to plan a session and how to get the outcomes that you wanted."

There are some key ideologies Wilshere and Ramsey share which might sound familiar - an emphasis on a high-technical level, possession-based football, hard work and intensity.

Wilshere encourages his team to get the ball to his best attacking players but is maybe Arteta-coded with his focus on "winning duels, second balls and competing physically".

He also sometimes allows his full-backs freedom - something else Arteta is renowned for at Arsenal to create unpredictability.

It is not just on the pitch where Wilshere takes care of the details.

When he walked into his post-match press conference at Wembley after winning his first trophy as a boss last season, he shook the hand of every reporter in the room - a small insight into his warm nature.

The ex-England international has also spoken about how he expresses both empathy and honesty with his players.

Ramsey made no bones about his plans when he joined Oxford in June either.

"I have a really clear way of playing, an identity that I want to create," he said at the time. "But that is built on clear principles first, underpinned by elite habits and behaviours."

That identity so far has been a team that likes to play out from the back, dominate possession and attack with verve.

Only Leicester (66%) and Stockport (62%) have had a higher average share of possession than Oxford (57%) in League One so far this season.

"I think it's evident to see why we're doing it," said Ramsey, who wants his team to take risks.

"It's not always going to be perfect. We're fully aware of that but those bits in the game where we can carve teams open - that outweighs the rest."

That approach sounds very Wenger-esque, with a sprinkling of Arteta when it comes to mindset and tweaking their tactics to suit the game on offer.

"Every week is different," he said. "But what I've liked so much about us is that we've always been able to adapt and figure out what's going on and ultimately win games of football."

Ramsey also exudes calm on the touchline, another trait perhaps borrowed from his former French boss.

Ramsey 'loving every second' of being Oxford boss

Learning from Arteta and inspiring youngsters - Wilshere on management

Back to the immediate matters in hand this weekend, and it could be a pivotal one.

"Some are talking about this game, when you put aside the Arsenal connections, as season-defining in League One," said BBC Radio Oxford sports presenter Jerome Sale.

Ramsey was keen to reiterate that this game was not about him and Wilshere.

"Far from it," he added. "It's about the players. Two good teams going head-to-head and hopefully everything on the pitch does the talking."

articles.title: USWNT vs. El Salvador Score, Highlights, Stats, Reaction from CONCACAF W Championship Quarter-Final
articles.summary: The W Championship gets underway with a direct 2027 World Cup berth on the line in the quarter-final. The loser will face Costa Rica with a second chance to earn a trip to Brazil.
articles.body:
Well, we sort of had a chance to take a breath after that late first-half onslaught.

It's safe to say there will be no upset and the USWNT will be going to Brazil. And while El Salvador hardly represents the kind of opposition the USWNT will face in the business end of that tournament, it was nonetheless impressive to see them make such a strong statement before halftime. El Salvador may have helped by playing a bit naively against the world's second-ranked team, but no matter.

The big story, though, will be Ashley Sanchez. Fresh of a career-best NWSL season, in which she won golden boot and MVP honors, she is back in the national team picture for the first time in a couple years. And she might just be playing well enough to disrupt the established Triple Espresso front three, even when Trinity Rodman is healthy.

articles.title: Luís Castro: "Guardiola no podría entrenar aquí porque no hace cambios o los hace en el 80"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Levante afirma que ha faltado efectividad en el ataque y entiende la exigencia de la afición
articles.summary: El entrenador del Levante afirma que ha faltado efectividad en el ataque y entiende la exigencia de la afición
articles.body: Luís Castro se “marcha del partido amargado” tras la derrota del Levante ante el Racing de Santander. El técnico luso ha apuntado que la combinación entre los cambios del rival y la lesión de Oriol ha condicionado el devenir del choque en la segunda parte. Además, ha destacado la actuación de Marc Santos en el partido y que Iván Romero ha jugado con una “rotura por contusión”. Buenos sesenta minutos “Después de perder 3 a 1 es difícil de explicar que podrías haber ganado. Podrías haber terminado la primera parte con dos o tres a cero. Necesitas mucho para hacer un gol y ellos, te hacen gol con muy poco. No pienso que el partido ha estado tan mal pero la verdad que lo que sientes es que te vas muy amargo. Te tienes que quedarte con las cosas buenas. Le diría a la grada que no debíamos hacer cambios. Guardiola no podría entrenar aquí porque no hace cambios o hace los cambios en los ochenta. ¿Mejoraste con los cambios? No, fuiste a peor. Uno de mis errores fue hacer los cambios. Quieres dar más pero quien entra, tiene que aportar. La perdida de Oriol nos dio mucho. Con él estabas controlando el partido. Con espacio el Racing es muy peligroso y no controlaste eso. El primer responsable soy yo, como siempre” Oriol o cambios “No pienso que es por una cosa pero pienso que las dos cosas están dentro del cambio del partido. Ellos salen muy bien con el balón. No ha sido solo por estas dos cosas pero pienso que ha sido por una combinación por las dos cosas. Desde esas dos cosas es verdad que no hemos tenido la clarividencia que teníamos” Mandi en el segundo gol del Racing “La acción empieza antes. Empieza en una jugada que ganas el primer balón y ellos ganan la segunda jugada y después, Zabiri que viene desde atrás, tú tienes que ir con todo el equipo para ayudar. Podríamos haber basculador un poco más y el remate es desde una zona lateral. Ha sido muy buen remate. La jugada no solo tiene que ver con Mandi” Cambios tras la lesión de Oriol “Primero hay que mirar el tiempo de lesión y a partir de ahí, ver las soluciones” Mensaje a Levante Fans “Yo no he dicho nada. Yo he escuchado lo que me querían decir, como hago en las derrotas. Yo me quedo en el campo porque soy el responsable número 1. Ellos quieren victorias y me decían que quieren más. Yo no miro a un equipo que no lo está intentando ni peleando. Si hubieras hecho eso goles en la primera mitad, hubieras ganado como en el partido contra el Real Betis. Yo comprendo la desilusión de la afición pero yo voy más allá. Si en los noventa minutos no hubiéramos atacado, sería otra cosa. Hay errores que hay que mirar y mejorar pero al final, si miras las oportunidades más claras y quien ha rematado más veces, hemos sido nosotros. Yo lo que digo es que necesitamos a la afición. Hoy con el 1-1, el estadio, para mí, no ha estado como de costumbre. Somos los que somos por ellos y este estadio tiene algo especial y no podemos perderlo” Marc Santos “Para mí ha sido uno de los mejores jugadores del equipo. Ha sido uno de los jugadores más tranquilos. No ha sido ninguna sorpresa para nosotros. Yo comprendo que se hable por su edad pero para mí ha sido uno de los mejores jugadores del equipo. Tanto Nacho como Marc, ha sido uno de los mejores. A mí no me importa la edad. Es bueno que ha renovado y que la cláusula es alta” Ivan Romero “Ivan ha jugado con una molestia. Eso dice mucho de él. En el último partido, cuando se ha quedado con problemas en la espalda, ha terminado con una rotura por contusión. Su partido dice mucho de él. Es uno de los que yo no hubiera quitado. Ha tenido oportunidad y ha generado oportunidades. Es bueno que ha marcado pero es mucho más que eso. Cuando él está dentro hace mucho mejores al resto” Preocupación por los resultados “Me gustaría tener más puntos. Yo estaría muy preocupado si no hubiéramos generado. Los dos ultimo partidos terminaste con más remates y con más oportunidades, solo que no terminas con más goles. Eso me da la sensación eu los resultados vendrán. Tampoco los jugadores que no meten gol es porque no quieren. Tuviste ocasiones que normalmente hacen gol. Yo sé que las preguntas se hacen por la tabla resultados, pero para mí, en los noventas minutos, el mejor equipo ha sido el Levante” Petar Ratkov “Pienso que recuperará de la molestia. No será grave pero vamos poco a poco. No metemos a los jugadores cuando tienen riesgo de lesión. Sabíamos el riesgo porque teníamos dos partidos muy cerca” Falta de eficacia “Nosotros tenemos calidad adelante y tenemos jugadores que hacen goles. Los jugadores que han venido necesitan tiempo y tu estás pendiente de los jugadores del año pasado y la comparación con el Racing es que ellos tenían dinero y nosotros, no. Los jugadores tienen calidad pero necesitan tiempo”

articles.title: What went wrong for Chelsea as Xabi Alonso's side slip to new low following dismal defeat at Nottingham Forest
articles.summary: Sky Sports analyses the decisions from Xabi Alonso that contributed to Chelsea's 3-2 defeat to Nottingham Forest; Wesley Fofana started despite his controversial interview, while Levi Colwill was dropped; Xabi Alonso called for fundamentals but Chelsea were outrun
articles.body:
"Everyone in the club and team, we need to stick together and go through this moment. We have to deal with it and we are responsible," Alonso told Sky Sports after the game, which marked their third successive defeat in the Premier League.

"It is a difficult moment for everyone at the club. For the team and the fans. Disappointed to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions.

"We can't stop. We are low in confidence. At this level you need to hold results and not concede so much. That is why we are losing."

Alonso now has as many losses in 15 games across all competitions as he did in 34 for Real Madrid (6). Since March, no side has more defeats in the top-flight than the Blues (14). And their problems are mounting by the day.

Here, Sky Sports analyses the decisions that contributed to the worrying defeat at the City Ground.

Despite the calls from Alonso to strip the game back to basics and get the fundamentals right, Chelsea felt short from minute one.

At the half-time interval, facing a 1-0 deficit and with zero shots on target, Chelsea had ran 3.8km less than Oliver Glasner's side.

The Forest boss was then quick to point out that they had outrun their opponents by 6km after the game. Yes, Chelsea had more possession, but they were also well behind in high-speed runs.

"I've seen one team jogging after the ball and one team sprinting after the ball and in this day and age, you cannot do that," said Jamie Redknapp.

"Distance covered is not always the barometer, but one thing is for sure, high-speed runs will tell you everything."

Fofana in the firing line - should he have started?

Starting Wesley Fofana in the same week the player had to apologise for his controversial interview, where he said he can "laugh about" the penalty miss that contributed to their Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool and contemplated retirement during injury spells at the club, was a bold move from Alonso. It did not pay off.

The tone was set early on. Fofana's first touches were heavily booed by the travelling Chelsea fans who had made the 130-mile journey in the cold and rain to watch their side slip to yet another dismal defeat.

The centre-back could only watch on as Igor Jesus volleyed in his stunning opener but was at the centre of attention, for all the wrong reasons, for the second.

After misjudging the ball while battling with former teammate Liam Delap, who caused problems all evening, Fofana rushed to atone for his error and fouled the striker in the penalty area.

Morgan Gibbs-White doubled the lead from the spot and ultimately the comeback, led by substitute Emmanuel Emegha, fell short.

He was cautioned for the challenge and eventually taken off for Levi Colwill, who was dropped by Alonso instead of Fofana, and the fans booed him once again.

"It didn't feel like a game for him tonight. He had a bad week with the podcast," said Jamie Redknapp after the game.

"By playing Fofana tonight, you created that. It was inevitable. He is lacking so much confidence; he needs some time.

"He is having a real difficult run of it at the moment."

After making the decision to drop Colwill, options at the centre of defence were limited with Maxence Lacroix and Reece James both sidelined.

Playing Josh Acheampong at centre-back and giving a rare start to Malo Gusto, an unused substitute on the night, seemed the more obvious choice but Alonso opted to play Moises Caicedo, arguably the best midfielder in the league, in the back four instead.

He was then tasked with dealing with a strike partnership of Delap and Igor Jesus. A difficult task for even the tallest of centre-backs, let alone a makeshift one standing at 5-foot-10.

He gave space to the Brazil striker for the opener and his presence in midfield was missed. He still led the way with 114 passes on the night, but Chelsea needed him in the middle of the park to deal with the likes of James McAtee and Xaver Schlager.

"They have bought players but if they do not sign a centre back, they cannot compete," said Redknapp after the game. He is right.

Emegha's impact was too little, too late

Alonso admitted that Emegha's performance after scoring twice off the bench was the lone positive for his side to take from their trip to the East Midlands. "For sure, he is having a good impact," he said. "He has done well. That is a positive."

He scored his first goal in the 4-1 defeat to Leeds United last time out but lost his place in the starting line-up on Friday.

Danny Welbeck, 36, was given the nod ahead of him and his performance mirrored the struggles Chelsea had as a unit.

Alonso called on the experience of Jordan Henderson and Welbeck to help weather their current struggles but it only whipped up the storm.

Welbeck was a bystander in the first half and had just seven touches before being replaced at the break, Emegha then scored with his first two to help spark hopes of a comeback.

His header for the second, holding off Jair Cunha, was one of the rare moments Chelsea matched the physicality of their opponents. He has to start moving forward without Joao Pedro available.

Alonso said the only way he knows how to address these issues is to attack them on the training ground. He has just five days to do that before they are put to the test against Crystal Palace, live on Sky Sports, who will be desperate for a win.

articles.title: It turns out Florida Gators coach Jon Sumrall is just as superstitious as his fanbase
articles.summary: Jon Sumrall made a last-minute switch away from the Florida Gators' blue helmets before the rivalry game with Florida State, and the gambit paid off.
articles.body: The Florida Gators and Florida State Seminoles played in a rare Friday afternoon game in the latest chapter of their storied rivalry. Although there were no stakes on the line as far as the College Football Playoff is concerned, these two teams hate each other to the point that the fear of losing is enough to get the juices flowing. Florida head coach Jon Sumrall was a newbie to this rivalry, but he certainly understood what a win (or a loss) in Tallahassee would do for him in year one. THESE ONCE-ANNUAL COLLEGE RIVALRIES USED TO DEFINE COLLEGE FOOTBALL AND NEED TO MAKE A COMEBACK ASAP You don't even need to hear him talk about it to know how much this game meant to him, as his actions spoke much louder than his words this week. All year, the Florida Gators were scheduled to wear blue helmets in their regular season finale against FSU. JON SUMRALL SAYS TEENAGE SON SENT HIM RUTHLESS TEXT BEFORE LEAVING FLORIDA'S LOSS TO SOUTH CAROLINA EARLY The blue helmets were nearly omnipresent in all of their promotional material leading up to the game, but there's just one problem. The Gators are 1-2 this season while wearing their blue lids, with the lone win coming against FCS program Campbell. Sumrall very likely knew about this, and being the superstitious psycho that he is, the Florida head honcho decided to call an audible. I'm sure all Gator fans can find comfort in knowing that their head football coach is literally the same as they are: a complete lunatic. URBAN MEYER JOINS DAN DAKICH, GUSHES ABOUT NEW FLORIDA HEAD COACH JON SUMRALL: 'I LOVE THAT GUY' We know head coaches are creatures of habit, but this takes things to a whole new level. Having watched Sumrall operate both professionally and as a fan, I can guarantee you he was acutely aware that his team stinks wearing blue helmets. Is there a strategic advantage to the switch? Absolutely not. But it's great to see the man trying anything he can to get an extra win this season. And his efforts were rewarded, as the Gators took down their arch rival FSU by a score of 26-10. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP So, maybe Sumrall was on to something after all.

articles.title: What Rick Stockstill said after losing to Florida
articles.summary: The FSU Seminoles lost to the Florida Gators on Friday. Here is what Rick Stockstill had to say after the game.
articles.body:
The Florida State Seminoles were unable to beat the Florida Gators on Friday night, losing 26-10 in Doak Campbell Stadium . They will finish the year 5-6, failing to make a bowl game for the third straight year.

FSU never led in the game and had another poor performance from Ashton Daniels, who threw two more interceptions. He briefly left the game in the third quarter with backup Kevin Sperry ending the drive with a touchdown. Despite Daniels' struggles, interim head coach Rick Stockstill said he never considered putting Sperry back in after Daniels returned.

Ashton was playing well. We got down there because of his feet. He was playing well. When Kevin came in we ran the ball three times and he scrambled around and found that, but again like I said last week, you gotta look at the thing in totality of what we see during the week. You don't ever make changes just to make a change. It's got to be a change where it's earned. You feel that the guy coming in is going to give you a better opportunity. And Ashton played well the first half and till he got hurt on that drive, and he missed a couple throws there in the fourth quarter. But no, I'd never thought about it. So, no sir.

Stockstill also talked about slowing down Jadan Baugh, their poor punting, Glenn Schumann, and more. Here are his full quotes after FSU lost to Florida.

Again, I appreciate everybody being here this afternoon. Give Florida credit; they did a nice job, got a good team and they whooped us. But I'm extremely proud of our team. We didn't always play good tonight. I asked them to leave their heart and soul on that field, play with great effort, competitiveness, and toughness, and to me they did that. I feel like they represented Florida State football program in a positive way these last four weeks. And we did a lot of good things, and I'm just proud of those guys and how they fought this afternoon. And obviously we're extremely short-handed, and nobody cares, but I'm proud of the guys, how they stepped up and competed tonight, and proud of what they've done these last four weeks. They've given us, me, Florida State football, everything I asked him to give. And so I wish them nothing but the best, and I'm so appreciative; I love them, I told them that in there. And disappointed we're not 4-0, but I'm not disappointed in how we played from an effort and competitive, toughness standpoint because these last four weeks they've done that, and that's what makes me proud the most.

On if he considered keeping Kevin Sperry in the game

On how proud he was of the defensive efforts

Yeah, I asked them to leave their heart and soul, and they did, and that was a really good Florida offensive football team that we went toe to toe with. And the goal line stand was great there early, and we really stopped the running game. I haven't looked at it yet, but I thought we did a really nice job stopping the run. And they got a quarterback scramble out there in that first drive of the third quarter. It was a big run for him, and then they hit a couple explosive plays in the passing game, but for the most part, I thought our defense was really, really good. Our kicking game, our punting game was horrendous, to be honest with you. Just put us in such bad field position, especially early in the game. And then if we got a stop, they punted us down there, so now our offense is in bad field position. So we just punted the ball not very well, obviously tonight, and that had a big impact on the game.

Yeah, tonight it probably looked like we were doing the roll kicks, but we weren't. They're supposed to be the deep spiral kicks, and they were just kind of short spiral kicks that rolled a little bit. But we just didn't play very well. And those guys, for the most part this year, have been very consistent. And tonight, they had a tough night tonight but those guys will bounce back next year.

Yeah, I have not talked to Glenn. He's preparing for his game tomorrow night, but whatever he asks me, that's up to him. Whatever he asks me. I'll be glad to give him my opinion, but he doesn't need my opinion. He knows what he's doing, and he'll come in here and do a fantastic job. But if he asks me, I'll be glad to share it, and like I told you, like I told you guys that first day, November 1st, you know that I love Florida State and all I want to do is help Florida State and help Florida State football. So if he asks me something, Corey, I'll be more than happy to answer his questions.

On bringing back the FSU spirit over the past month

I'm gonna answer that with I hope. I hope I impacted these players, this fan base, the supporters, our football team, our coaches. I hope I injected some life into them, some positivity, some hope, and belief, because Florida State; we've suffered 3 straight years now, and it's not fun, and Florida State is so much better than what it's been. I only want Florida State to be great again, and I hope in these 4 weeks that I did give Florida State fans and this university and this program and these players hope, and because I have no doubt Glenn Coach Schuman, coming in here, and that Florida State will be in the playoffs next year. I really believe that because I just believe so much in Florida State.

On if there are the pieces in place for this team to take a step next year

Yeah, it's a tough question to answer because they've got decisions to make too. So you don't really know who's coming back. We lose whatever came out of there this afternoon, 20 seniors to graduation, and then there's going to be portal guys and all that kind of stuff, so it's hard to put your finger on what this team is going to look like here in a month. Then, coach Schumann (Glenn Schuman), schematically, what does he want his defense to look like? What does his offence? What's his kicking game, special teams look like? So it's really kind of a hard question to answer because you don't know who's coming back.

On going for it on fourth down late in the game

I'm always a believer that points are a lot more important than yards. And you don't get points just because you outgained them in yards. But really, we went for it on fourth down when we threw the touchdown pass there. I didn't think there was enough, at that point in the game. I didn't know if there was going to be enough possessions with the score of the game to kick a field goal. And then, there's 11-plus minutes left in the game and it was fourth and six I believe, maybe fourth and seven, and we were on the minus side of the field. And I felt like if we could punt it the way our defense was playing, if we could punt them down there, get them inside the 10, inside the 15, if we could get a three-andout, then we'd still get the ball back with, I think we were down seven at the time with 10 minutes left in the game. So I thought there was enough time, but we didn't get a very good punt. Now they start on the minus-31, I think it was, 32. And then after that it was just the timing of everything and the score in the game that there weren't going to be enough possessions. When we were down there, way back there on the minus-25 or whatever that was when we went for it, there just wasn't enough time left to get enough possessions to get back in the game.

I've always taken the high road, Cory. But this defense this year, this defense the last 4 weeks, is a heck of a lot better than the defense played against Florida last year, and we tackled better. We didn't have mistakes, alignment mistakes, missed assignments. Ernie (Ernie Sims), T Knight (Terrance Knighton), Nick (Nick Williams), Blue (Blue Adams) and Greg (Greg Moss), those guys did a great job these 4 weeks and had our guys in the right position. Their effort was great. Defense is about effort more so than anything, and they were tough. They're physical, and I'm proud of the defense and what they did out there, man, because that's a big-time back; he's going to make a bunch of money in the NFL one day, and I'm proud of our defense, and to me that was the difference. We tackled better than we did last year. We didn't make as many mental mistakes, missed assignments. A lot better defense.

articles.title: Bianchi: Jon Sumrall has made Florida football fun again! Can Glenn Schumann do the same at FSU?
articles.summary: TALLAHASSEE – There was a time when an 8-4 football season at the University of Florida would get you fired. Nowadays – at least next season – it might get y...
articles.body:
TALLAHASSEE – There was a time when an 8-4 football season at the University of Florida would get you fired.

Nowadays – at least next season – it might get you into the College Football Playoff.

And, in the case of Jon Sumrall, it will get him a standing ovation during the offseason booster club circuit.

As that great college football analyst Bob Dylan once said, "The times, they are a-changin' ".

Thank goodness, so have the Florida Gators.

With Friday's 26-10 victory over Florida State at Doak Campbell Stadium, Sumrall put the finishing touches on a regular season that wasn't necessarily spectacular in the standings but was positively transformational in spirit.

After four years of mundane, monotonous, mind-numbing Billy Ball, that alone is cause for celebration. Watching the Gators under Billy Napier was like going to a fireworks show and being handed a sparkler.

In comparison, Sumrall brought the dynamite.

Even so, Florida's first-year head coach didn't seem like he was in any mood to light up the victory cigars that were being passed out after Saturday's victory.

"If anybody thinks we've done anything worth celebrating, they're absolutely idiotic," Sumrall said. "This is a step in the right direction, there's signs of life, but we are not where we need to be yet. There's been a lot of growth, but a lot of growth is still needed. But I'm not at peace with 8-4. That's not where I want to live."

Maybe not, but it's a pretty dadgum good starter home. The Gators finished 8-4, with victories over three teams – Ole Miss, Texas and Kentucky – ranked among the top 11 in the country when Florida played them.

Yes, I know, there was a time when Gator Nation turned up its collective nose at 8-4 seasons. Hell, Ron Zook essentially got run out of Gainesville for winning eight games a year.

But the college football world in which Zook coached is as antiquated as the flip phone the Zooker carried in his pocket. Starting next season, with the anticipated expansion to a 24-team playoff, an 8-4 SEC team will have a legitimate shot at playing for a national championship.

Conference realignment has created bigger, deeper, more treacherous power conferences. Expanded league schedules mean fewer Saturdays spent fattening up on directional universities. The transfer portal and NIL have redistributed talent throughout the sport.

It's becoming increasingly difficult for the Ohio States and Alabamas of the world to stockpile future NFL players on their second-string units and steamroll their way through the regular season.

Nine-and-three is becoming the new 11-1.

Eight-and-four might soon be the new 10-2.

The sooner college football fans recalibrate their expectations, the happier their autumns will be.

Speaking of recalibrating expectations, how depressing is it that the Florida-Florida State game is now being played on Black Friday?

This rivalry used to determine who was going to play for a national championship. Now it's being squeezed in between doorbuster specials and discounts on air fryers.

Believe me, I understood why UCF and USF used to customarily play on Black Friday. Back then, they were two Group of Five programs looking for national exposure were wise to take advantage of a relatively uncluttered television window.

But Florida and Florida State should never, ever feel the need to seek out exposure.

Can you imagine Michigan and Ohio State playing on Black Friday? Actually, don't answer that. The television networks have already purchased college football's soul. It's probably only a matter of time before they ask for the mineral rights.

Still, consider the sad state of our state's signature sporting event: Last year, Florida came into this game with interim coach Billy Gonzales after firing Napier and beat a sinking Florida State program under Mike Norvell. This year, FSU came into the game with interim coach Rick Stockstill after firing Norvell.

The rivalry has gone from national championship implications to severance package negotiations.

Florida State can only hope its new coach, Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann, can administer the same sort of adrenaline shot Sumrall injected into the Gators. Judging by Friday's game, the Seminoles desperately need it. It got so bad at one point Friday that FSU fans began booing their own punters – two of whom combined for seven punts for an average 33 yards per punt. In fact, they were more like chip shots than punts.

This is the sort of downtrodden program Schumann inherited. Three seasons of football futility have coincided with an increasingly precarious financial situation in Tallahassee. You can restructure debt, renegotiate agreements, solicit donations and concoct all sorts of creative accounting mechanisms.

But there's one financial instrument that has historically worked better than all the others at Florida State and every other institution of higher earning, er, learning:

The quickest way for FSU to start digging itself out of its financial hole is to start making its way up the ACC standings. And, quite frankly, that shouldn't require some sort of college football miracle. With all due respect to Wake Forest, Louisville and Duke, there is no earthly reason those programs should be looking down at Florida State in the conference hierarchy.

Bobby Bowden used to treat the top of ACC standings like his own personal reserved parking space. The Seminoles need to reclaim it and reclaim it quickly.

What Sumrall has demonstrated in Gainesville is that rebuilding a football program no longer has to be a painstaking, five-year archaeological excavation. In today's college football, the right coach, the right investments and the right personnel decisions can change the trajectory of a program almost overnight.

Sumrall hasn't won a championship. He hasn't even won nine games. But he has given Gator fans something they haven't had nearly enough of over the last several years: A reason to spend the offseason looking forward instead of looking backward.

And wouldn't it be wonderful if, a couple of years from now, Schumann has done the same thing in Tallahassee? Maybe then Florida-Florida State will once again be too big to be treated as a Black Friday doorbuster special.

Maybe then this rivalry will be put on the appropriate shelf where it belongs:

Among college football's premium merchandise.

Email me at mbianchi@orlandosentinel.com . Hit me up on social media @BianchiWrites and listen to my radio show "Game On" every weekday from 3 to 6 p.m. on FM 96.9, AM 740 and 969TheGame.com/listen .

articles.title: Gophers' first-half woes continue with another dreadful start against Wisconsin
articles.summary: Minnesota's first-half performance against Wisconsin was an absolute disaster.
articles.body:
The Gophers have had a handful of poor first halves in 2026, and Friday's showing against Wisconsin was among the worst. An early 21-3 halftime deficit put them in a massive hole against the Badgers.

Minnesota wasn't able to build on the offensive momentum it had in its final home game against Northwestern. Drake Lindsey began the game 3 of 8 for just 24 yards. The Gophers' offense was outgained 298-39. Minnesota showing up unprepared on the road has become far too common a trend under P.J. Fleck.

Wisconsin had 16 first downs compared to one for Minnesota. The Badgers had 153 rushing yards compared to 15 for the Gophers. The entire box score looked abysmal, and Minnesota looked like a team already looking ahead to 2027.

After going winless on the road in 2025, Minnesota's quartet of poor first halves might be the theme of the 2026 season. The Gophers will look to have a different fate in the second half against the Badgers.
